item.text: Although both cultures observe the same cycle of light and darkness, they may organize time around different activities, environments, and beliefs. A farming community might distinguish periods by sunrise, midday heat, and evening work, while an urban society might emphasize clock hours, work shifts, and commuting. Religious practices, meal patterns, and seasonal changes can also shape meaningful divisions. Thus, the natural cycle provides a shared foundation, but each culture interprets it according to its social routines and priorities.
